The fixed-dose combination of acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) and ethoheptazine was historically prescribed for the short-term relief of mild-to-moderate pain, musculoskeletal disorders, and headaches. It combines a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with a phenazepane-family opioid analgesic to target pain via multiple mechanisms.

 +1

In June 2026, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) in India officially prohibited the manufacture, sale, and distribution of this combination because it poses risks to human health and lacks scientific rationality, especially given that safer alternatives are readily available. It has also been unavailable in the United States and other major markets for decades.
TeamLease RegTech
 +2
Historical Uses and Mechanism
When it was actively marketed, the combination was utilized for its dual-action therapeutic properties:
Mild-to-Moderate Pain Relief: It was primarily given to treat acute tension headaches, dental or postoperative pain, and transient musculoskeletal pain.
Muscle Relaxation: It helped alleviate discomfort associated with muscle spasms and joint stiffness.
ScienceDirect.com
 +3
The individual components functioned as follows:
Acetylsalicylic Acid (Aspirin): A non-selective cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2) inhibitor. It acts peripherally to block the production of prostaglandins, thereby reducing inflammation, swelling, and localized pain signaling.

An expert evaluation concluded that combining these two agents did not offer a rational medical advantage. Gliclazide combined with chromium picolinate is primarily prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults. It is used alongside diet and lifestyle changes to improve glycemic control when standard single-drug therapies are insufficient.

This combination works by tackling blood sugar management from two different angles:
Gliclazide: An oral antidiabetic medication belonging to the sulfonylurea class. It works by stimulating the beta cells in the pancreas to produce and release more insulin, which effectively lowers circulating blood glucose levels.
Diabetes UK
 +2
Chromium Picolinate: A mineral supplement included to enhance insulin sensitivity. It helps the body's cells respond more effectively to insulin, allowing them to absorb glucose from the bloodstream more efficiently.
Healthline

Medical Context and Regulatory Status
While the individual components are well-known, fixed-dose combinations of gliclazide and chromium picolinate have faced scrutiny. Major global diabetes guidelines do not typically recommend routine chromium supplementation because clinical trials have shown inconsistent evidence regarding its added benefit. In fact, medical regulatory authorities in certain regions (such as India) have previously banned specific fixed-dose combinations of gliclazide and chromium picolinate, declaring them therapeutically unjustified due to a lack of proven additional clinical advantage over using gliclazide alone.

blocks.text: Gliclazide combined with chromium picolinate is primarily prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults. It is used alongside diet and lifestyle changes to improve glycemic control when standard single-drug therapies are insufficient.
This combination works by tackling blood sugar management from two different angles:

blocks.label: Gliclazide
blocks.text: An oral antidiabetic medication belonging to the sulfonylurea class. It works by stimulating the beta cells in the pancreas to produce and release more insulin, which effectively lowers circulating blood glucose levels.

blocks.label: Chromium Picolinate
blocks.text: A mineral supplement included to enhance insulin sensitivity. It helps the body's cells respond more effectively to insulin, allowing them to absorb glucose from the bloodstream more efficiently.
Medical Context and Regulatory Status

While the individual components are well-known, fixed-dose combinations of gliclazide and chromium picolinate have faced scrutiny. Major global diabetes guidelines do not typically recommend routine chromium supplementation because clinical trials have shown inconsistent evidence regarding its added benefit. In fact, medical regulatory authorities in certain regions (such as India) have previously banned specific fixed-dose combinations of gliclazide and chromium picolinate, declaring them therapeutically unjustified due to a lack of proven additional clinical advantage over using gliclazide alone.

However, you will still frequently find chromium picolinate combined in triple-drug formulations that include Metformin alongside Gliclazide, as metformin works synergistically to control insulin resistance.

blocks.label: Take with Food
blocks.text: This medication should be taken exactly as prescribed by your doctor, typically with or immediately before breakfast.

blocks.text: Because gliclazide actively pushes your pancreas to release insulin, skipping meals after taking it can cause your blood sugar to drop dangerously low (hypoglycemia). Always carry a fast-acting sugar source (like candy, glucose tablets, or fruit juice) with you.

blocks.label: Skin and Soft Tissue Infections

blocks.label: Post-Surgical & Post-Traumatic Recovery
blocks.text: Used following surgical procedures or trauma to prevent secondary bacterial infections and significantly reduce swelling inside the cheeks, mouth, or limbs.

blocks.label: Dental Infections
blocks.text: Manages severe tooth abscesses and jaw swelling before or after dental extractions.

blocks.label: Ear, Nose, and Throat (ENT) Infections
